newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FENCING-GOLDEN NIGHT FOR CUBA.
newsitem.headline: FENCING-GOLDEN NIGHT FOR CUBA.

text.p: Cuba's women made a mockery of the world rankings on a marvellous night for the Republic in the world fencing championships on Thursday.
They took both gold and silver in the women's epee and added a team gold in the men's epee to dominate the day's proceedings.

In the women's final Miraida Garcia-Soto, ranked a lowly 17th in the world scored a 15-12 victory over compatriot Zuleidys Ortiz-Puente, ranked 26th, to claim Cuba's first women's fencing world title.

On the way to the final Ortiz-Puente beat Olympic gold medallist and world number one Laura Flessel of France while Garcia-Soto accounted for Olympic bronze medallist Gyongyi Szalay of Hungary in the semifinals.
An unusual feature of the final was that at the intervals the two Cubans sat together at the centre of the piste with their coach.
Cuban joy was complete when their three-man team of Ivan Trevejo Perez, Carlos Pedroso and Nelson Loyola comfortably overcame Germany 45-34 in the team epee final.

Trevejo Perez won each of his three bouts against Germany's Michael Flegler, Arnd Schmitt and Elmar Borrmann to lead the way as Cuba emulated their achievement at the 1995 world championships in The Hague when they took the team foil gold.
